title: Pony.ai unveils autonomous electric truck for logistics fleets
contentZh:
Pony.ai has unveiled an autonomous electric truck for logistics fleets, developed with GAC Commercial Vehicle for freight supply chains.Unveiled at IAA Transportation 2026, this Level 4 (L4) heavy rig marks the fourth-generation (Gen-4) iteration of Pony.ai’s Robotruck platform. It builds on GAC Commercial Vehicle’s T9 battery-electric truck architecture, with mass production set to start later this year. Initial routes will target long-haul freight, dedicated logistics corridors, and port transport operations.He Xing, VP of Pony.ai and Head of its Robotruck business, said: “The global debut of the T9 autonomous heavy-duty truck with GAC Commercial Vehicle marks another important step in accelerating the mass production and commercial deployment of Pony.ai’s Robotrucks.“Looking ahead, we will deepen our collaboration with GAC Commercial Vehicle, continue advancing volume production and deployment of the T9 Robotrucks, and bring our jointly-developed autonomous trucking solutions to markets around the world.”Pony.ai Robotruck sensor architecture and kit costsAn automotive-grade autonomous driving kit (ADK) equips the vehicle with nine lidars, three millimetre-wave radars, and 13 cameras, providing complete 360-degree sensing around the truck.  Hardware expenses for the system have fallen sharply. The bill-of-materials cost for the Gen-4 ADK is down 70 percent compared with the previous iteration, and transportation operating costs per ton-kilometre are projected to drop by 30 percent.Energy efficiency is paired with aerodynamic refinements. Pony.ai’s control algorithms work alongside the T9 cab’s 0.4 drag coefficient (Cd) to reduce energy consumption by 10 percent compared with conventional haulage trucks.Virtual Driver compute and chassis redundancyThe Gen-4 Robotruck shares its central domain controller with Pony.ai’s seventh-generation (Gen-7) robotaxis, running the company’s unified ‘Virtual Driver’ software.Engineers paired the software stack directly with GAC Commercial Vehicle’s drive-by-wire chassis. For reliable driverless operation, full hardware backups are integrated across steering, braking, power supply, computing, sensors, and communications.Development grew out of a strategic agreement signed on 16 April, with both partners completing vehicle validation in five months to reach production readiness.  Autonomous truck production and global logistics deploymentPony.ai has pursued autonomous trucking development since 2018, assembling a fleet portfolio across heavy- and light-duty platforms.The company’s commercial logistics programme involves vehicle manufacturers and transport operators spanning bulk commodity shipping, port logistics, urban delivery, and long-haul line haulage. The platform applies identical core software across passenger robotaxis and heavy transport vehicles.Following the initial domestic production run this year, Pony.ai plans to expand its Robotruck operations into European and Middle Eastern markets over the ne

xt two years.
